raw_response:
Alright, let me sit down and think through this year on my 4.1 mu.

I'm 68 now, been farming this land since I was a teenager. My wife helps me when she can, and my son comes back from town to help at harvest — that's our three people, but really it's me and the old woman doing most of the daily work. 4.1 mu isn't much, but it's what feeds us and brings in a little cash.

**Wheat (winter, going in now-ish mentally for next October)**

I plant the same as always — early October, after I clear the maize stalks. I buy seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, whatever variety they're selling that year, usually Jimai or Shiluan something. About 15 kg of seed per mu, nothing fancy. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — one bag of 15-15-15 per mu, that's about 50 jin, so roughly 12 kg N base. The extension guy keeps telling us to split the nitrogen, and I do listen some — at jointing in March, if the wheat looks a bit pale, I topdress 10-12 kg of urea per mu. That's roughly 5 kg N more, so maybe 17 kg N total. I don't measure exactly, I eyeball it.

Irrigation — I give it winter water in December if it's dry, then jointing water in March, then grain-fill water around early May. Three times usually. Four if spring is dry. Each irrigation costs me 40-50 yuan per mu with the well electricity and my time, so I don't waste it.

Herbicide in spring for the weeds — one spray. I don't spray much else. Harvest early June with the combine — I pay someone, 60 yuan per mu. Expected yield maybe 450 kg/mu, I've hit 500 in good years but 400 is more honest for me.

**Maize (summer, right after wheat)**

Tight turnaround — I've got maybe 3-5 days after wheat harvest. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu or whatever the shop pushes, about 60-70 yuan per mu. I don't till — I just use no-till planting, pay the custom planter operator 30 yuan per mu to drill it straight into the stubble. I'm too old to plow, and everyone does no-till now anyway.

Base fertilizer goes in with the planter — compound, about one bag per mu again (12 kg N). I topdress urea at big bell stage (around late July) — 10-12 kg urea per mu, maybe 5 kg N more. So about 17 kg N total again. Same as wheat, habit.

Irrigation — usually one time right after planting to get it up, maybe one more if July is dry. Herbicide once after planting. Corn borer — I used to worry about it but the new seeds handle it better, I skip insecticide most years. Harvest late September with combine, 70 yuan per mu. Expected yield around 500 kg/mu.

**The money side**

On 4.1 mu I'll spend something like 2,200-2,500 yuan total on inputs across both crops. Wheat sells for ~1.3 yuan/kg, maize ~1.2 yuan/kg. After costs I maybe clear 3,000-3,500 yuan from the whole year. That's not much, but the grain also feeds us, and I get the subsidy from the government. My son sends money, that's how we really live.

I don't experiment much. At 68, with 4 mu, there's no room to gamble. What worked last year works this year.
